The c_operationsFC array has 8 entries (0x00-0x07) in non-DEBUG, plus a 9th "termination" entry in DEBUG mode (index 8).

GetOpInfo(opcode) for opcode with high byte 0xFC returns &c_operationsFC[opcode & 0xFF]. So if the extended opcode byte (the byte after 0xFC) is >= 8 (non-DEBUG) or >= 9 (DEBUG), it reads out of bounds.

There are two code paths to reach GetOpInfo with a 0xFC opcode:

Path A (d_m3CompileExtendedOpcode defined):
- Read_opcode reads just 0xFC (single byte) since the #ifndef d_m3CompileExtendedOpcode block is skipped.
- In Compile_BlockStatements, opcode=0xFC, GetOpInfo(0xFC) returns &c_operations[0xFC] which is the [0xFC]=M3OP(...Compile_ExtendedOpcode) entry. That's valid (c_operations has up to 0xFC). opinfo->compiler = Compile_ExtendedOpcode.
- Compile_ExtendedOpcode reads the next byte as `opcode` (u8), then i_opcode = (0xFC << 8) | opcode = 0xFC00 | opcode.
- Then GetOpInfo(i_opcode) is called. i_opcode >> 8 = 0xFC, so returns &c_operationsFC[opcode & 0xFF]. If opcode >= 8 (or 9 in DEBUG), OOB read.

- In Compile_BlockStatements, GetOpInfo(opcode) where opcode>>8 = 0xFC, returns &c_operationsFC[opcode & 0xFF]. If nextbyte >= 8/9, OOB.
